title: Pick the undo
prompt:
Your most recent commit on `main`, `8f1e2aa Move nav into header`, broke the mobile menu. You pushed it an hour ago and two teammates have already pulled. `git status` shows a clean working tree.

```text
8f1e2aa (HEAD -> main, origin/main) Move nav into header
c39be11 Add projects page
b2e04f3 Add navigation bar with base styles
```

Which command should you run before pushing again?
hints: Ask where the mistake lives: your files, the index, a local commit, or a shared commit?
Anything that changes `8f1e2aa` itself would need a force-push to a branch others have pulled.
You want to add history, not rewrite it.
explanation: The bad commit is already shared, so rewriting it (amend or reset) would force everyone else to repair their history. `git revert HEAD` adds a new commit that applies the exact opposite of `8f1e2aa`; push it normally and your teammates get the fix with an ordinary pull. Later you can fix the nav properly on a branch and bring the move back through a pull request.

a.why: This deletes a commit your teammates already have. Their next push can bring it back, and the force-push may wipe out anything pushed in the meantime.

b.why: Correct. The new commit cancels `8f1e2aa` without rewriting shared history.

c.why: The working tree is clean, so there's nothing to restore. The bug is inside a commit, and only a new commit can undo it publicly.

d.why: Amend replaces the latest commit with a new ID, which is a rewrite of a pushed commit and would need a force-push.
